narrative:
Your application was denied because the model estimated a 95.9% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That is a very high risk estimate, and in this process it was treated as enough to reject your law-school application.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you are in the top decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile. In this model’s pattern, that standing still pushed the prediction toward failure, even though it may seem favorable. The second most influential factor was your LSAT score of 26, well below the accepted-student average of about 37; this also pushed strongly toward failure. Your first-year class standing, also top decile versus an accepted average near the sixth decile, was the third most important factor and likewise pushed toward failure. Together, these academic indicators outweighed other information and produced the denial.

You should ask admissions whether you can review or correct the record, especially your class-rank and LSAT data. If a retake is allowed, prepare for and retake the LSAT, and submit any updated grades or rank information. Ask whether conditional admission, an interview, or a written explanation could be considered. Also speak with a pre-law advisor about schools and support programs where your profile is a better fit.
